message.reasoning:
We need to generate high-quality unit test code for NumericIndicator.min(Indicator<Num>) covering basic functionality and exception handling as per JSON cases. Already some tests exist for min with constant indicator and with mocked indicator. Need to add tests covering constant indicator higher, lower, same instance, mixed values, null, different series, shorter series.

We must use JUnit5, Mockito. Use existing framework: class NumericIndicator_min_Test with @BeforeAll etc. Already contains two tests: min_withConstantIndicator_returnsCorrectMinimum (but uses numeric.min(constant) which is overload with Number, not the Indicator version). That test is for min(Number). But we need tests for min(Indicator) with ConstantIndicator etc.

We can add parameterized test for basic functionality with ConstantIndicator values. Use ConstantIndicator<Num>. Provide series same as closePrice. For same instance case, use numeric.min(numeric) and assert same values (and maybe same object? Implementation returns NumericIndicator.of(BinaryOperation.min(this, other)). Might produce new instance but values equal. We'll assert values equal.

Mixed values: constant 0 with series containing negative and positive. Our series currently 0-9 only positive. Need series with negative values. Could create new series for this test. Use MockBarSeries with values -5, -2, 0, 3, 5 etc. Provide closePrice indicator.

Exception tests: null indicator should throw NullPointerException. Use assertThrows.

Different BarSeries: create second series with different values, create ConstantIndicator based on that series? Actually ConstantIndicator takes Num constant, not series. For series mismatch, we need an indicator based on different BarSeries, e.g., new ClosePriceIndicator(otherSeries). Then numeric.min(otherIndicator) should throw IllegalArgumentException per BinaryOperation.min validation. We'll test that.

Shorter series: create other series with fewer bars, use ClosePriceIndicator of that series, then call min and attempt to get value at index beyond shorter length expecting IndexOutOfBoundsException. Since min returns NumericIndicator that delegates to both; calling getValue at index that exists only in longer series will cause other.getValue(index) to throw IOBE. So test that.

Make sure to import needed classes: ConstantIndicator, ClosePriceIndicator, etc.

We need to use reflection only if min method is private, but it's public.

Implement parameterized test using @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource maybe for constants.

But we need separate test groups.

Let's write code.

We'll keep existing tests unchanged, add new tests.

Note: NumericIndicator.min(Indicator) method returns NumericIndicator. Use NumericIndicator.of(closePrice).min(otherIndicator).

Make sure to use numFunction for conversion.

Implement tests.
